# Sealed binlog fixtures

From the repository root, run `python3 internal/sidecar/testdata/generate_binlogs.py` and then `go run internal/sidecar/testdata/generate_retention_binlogs.go` to regenerate these deterministic MySQL v4 wire-format fixtures. They contain a format-description event, previous GTIDs, a GTID event, an autocommit query, and a stop event, with event positions and CRC32 checksums. Tests parse every event with checksum verification enabled, including the final stop event. `tagged-transaction.bin` adds a MySQL 8.4 tagged GTID serialized with the upstream parser's field format; it contains `restore_tag:11`, distinct from an untagged transaction with the same number.

These small fixtures are generated bytes, not captures from a running MySQL server. `incarnation-a.bin` and `incarnation-b.bin` model two streams at the same site. The three original fixtures have equal sizes. `same-header.bin` has A's previous GTIDs and timestamps but B's statement bytes, demonstrating why a metadata summary cannot identify immutable content.

`review-order-a.bin`, `review-order-b.bin`, and `review-clock-b.bin` are deterministic CRC32-valid review reproductions. A contains transaction 11 after predecessors 1–10; B contains transaction 12 after predecessors 1–11. The order pair has equal header times and reverse digest order; the clock variant has a one-second backward header clock. They test causal replay ordering, not a live MySQL replay.

`empty-sealed.bin` contains only FDE/PREVIOUS_GTIDS/STOP. `compressed-transaction.bin` keeps GTID 11 outside a ZSTD TRANSACTION_PAYLOAD_EVENT containing its query body. Both have valid outer CRC32 checksums; the compressed fixture uses MySQL payload size/type/uncompressed-size headers and checksum-free inner events.

`native/` contains real MySQL 8.4 captures and mysqlbinlog output goldens,
with an opt-in native-tool equivalence test and an ordinary CI fixture check.
See [native capture and oracle instructions](native/README.md).
